title: How dogs and cats came to live with humans: wolves and hunter-gatherers, wildcats and early grain farmers

sources.title: Out of the desert, on to the sofa

sources.publisher: Frontiers in Psychology (via PubMed Central, U.S. National Library of Medicine)
sources.title: The human-initiated model of wolf domestication – An expansion based on human-dingo relations in Aboriginal Australia

facts.text: Today's dogs come from an ancient wolf population that has died out; dogs and modern gray wolves share that lost ancestor.
Leading researchers place the start of dog domestication among hunter-gatherers, before farming began.
Scientists still disagree about when, where, and how wolves turned into dogs.
One theory: wolves that were less afraid of people followed human groups to eat their food waste and slowly became tame.
A rival theory: hunter-gatherers took young wolf pups from dens and raised them in their camps.
People later bred dogs for jobs such as guarding, hunting, herding, and hauling loads, so dogs differ greatly in size and shape.
House cats descend from the Near Eastern wildcat (Felis silvestris lybica) of the Middle East's deserts.
When early farmers in the Fertile Crescent stored grain, mice moved in to eat it, and the mice drew wildcats to the villages.
Cats most likely chose to live near people on their own, so they largely domesticated themselves.
Unlike dogs, cats were not bred for tasks; the typical house cat keeps the wild body plan of its ancestor.
Many domestic cats can survive without humans and keep their hunting skills.

notes: 混合題 mixed-top-01 用（2026-10-09 線上查證，只取事實、不取原句）。狗的馴化方式有爭議（跟著營地撿食物的狼 vs. 獵人帶回狼崽），選文兩種都寫成「有些科學家認為／另一些人認為」，不寫成定論；狗的祖先寫成「已經不存在的古代狼群」（不是今天的灰狼）。狗比黑猩猩更會看手勢的研究有爭議，選文不用。
